name: Deep Research
description: Multi-step web research with persistent document storage
intent_examples: do deep research on quantum computing
research the latest advances in robotics
compare GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus on coding
write a report on the GPU market
give me a thorough analysis of the M4 Pro chip

systemPromptAddition:
## Deep Research

Use one execution path by default. Ordinary news requests, comparisons, broad or comprehensive research, and deep dives do not authorize extra agents merely because they could be divided.

### Picking the right tool
- Answer a simple factual question directly when confident; otherwise use one targeted search.
- Use `research_search` for every ordinary research request, including broad, deep, comprehensive, current-news, comparison, and multi-source work. Search, read, synthesize, and lead with the answer instead of dumping raw results.
- Use `deep_research_parallel` only when the user explicitly asks for parallelism, fan-out, or multiple agents. An explicit uncounted request uses 2-4 angles. If the user gives an exact agent count, route the complete outcome through `spawn_worker` so that count is preserved; do not call `deep_research_parallel` directly.
- Never infer parallel authorization from words such as deep, broad, comprehensive, latest, compare, all, or multiple sources.

### Research quality
- Cite sources inline for specific factual claims and flag conflicts or uncertainty.
- Put a 2-5 sentence summary first, then supporting detail, then a Sources section with numbered URLs and the research date.
- Keep chat concise when the full report is saved.

### Ordinary single-path workflow
1. Call `research_search` with the appropriate depth.
2. Use targeted `web_search` or `fetch_url` follow-ups only when the first result has a concrete gap.
3. Synthesize a clear markdown report with citations.
4. Call `list_research` before saving. If a matching document exists, call `get_research`, merge old and new findings, then call `update_research` with its current version. Otherwise call `save_research`.
5. Present a concise summary and mention the saved document.

### Explicit parallel workflow
Call `deep_research_parallel` once only for an explicit uncounted parallel request. It plans 2-4 distinct angles, waits for them, synthesizes one report, and saves it. Present its summary and document id; do not save it again.

### Updating and retrieving research
Before `update_research`, call `get_research`, preserve unique valid findings, replace outdated material, deduplicate sources, and pass the returned version as `expected_version`. On a stale-version error, reread and re-merge. For past research, use `list_research` then `get_research` and present the requested material.

function.name: deep_research_parallel
function.description: Parallel multi-angle research, available only when the user explicitly asks for parallel or multiple agents. With an explicit uncounted request it decomposes the topic into 2-4 angles, runs bounded research agents, synthesizes their findings, and auto-saves the document. Exact-count requests must go through spawn_worker so the count is preserved. For every ordinary deep, comprehensive, broad, news, comparison, or single-facet request, use research_search instead; the server falls back to that single execution path when parallelism was not explicitly requested.

topic.description: The research topic or question to investigate comprehensively

depth.description: Depth per sub-angle (if the planner decomposes the topic). Default: standard. Only affects the fallback single-pass path — parallel workers always use standard depth internally.

function.name: research_search
function.description: Perform a multi-step web research search on a topic. Runs multiple search queries to build comprehensive findings. Returns structured results with sources and suggested follow-up queries. Use 'quick' for overviews, 'standard' for solid coverage, 'deep' for exhaustive research with page fetches. Optionally include specific URLs to fetch and incorporate as primary sources.

topic.description: The research topic or question to investigate

depth.description: Research depth: quick (3 searches), standard (6 searches), deep (10 searches + URL fetches). Default: standard

urls.description: Optional list of specific URLs to fetch and include as primary sources in the research

function.name: save_research
function.description: Save a research document as a persistent markdown file for the user. The document can be retrieved later by the user at any time.

content.description: Full markdown content of the research document

tags.description: Tags for categorization and search (e.g. ['quantum computing', 'physics', '2026'])

function.name: list_research
function.description: List the user's saved research documents. Optionally filter by a search query that matches against titles and tags.

query.description: Optional search query to filter documents by title or tags

function.name: get_research
function.description: Retrieve the full content of a saved research document by its ID.

function.name: update_research
function.description: Update an existing research document with merged content. Call get_research immediately first and pass its version as expected_version; stale writes are rejected so newer research is not overwritten.

documentId.description: The ID of the document to update

content.description: The new/merged markdown content to replace the existing document

expected_version.description: Current version returned by the immediately preceding get_research call

tags.description: Updated tags (optional — keeps existing tags if omitted)

function.name: delete_research
function.description: Delete a saved research document. Ask the user for confirmation before calling this.
